checks.detail: Induction on a simple O_E submodule is valid without semisimplicity of the full module. An isotropic simple module contributes its order and leaves D-perp/D; a nonisotropic simple module splits orthogonally. Conjugate adjointness forces its prime to be conjugation-fixed and the host unramifiedness makes the residue involution nontrivial. The CA3 norm Gauss sum has the negative inert sign, including residue characteristic two. The same signed lambda is used throughout; its square identity is proved in the induction.

The rational lattice is the actual rational intersection of the completed host-scaled Hom lattice. Density and finite completion justify self-duality and integral quotient cardinalities. For u(x)=h^{-1}xg the correct finite-action lattice is u^{-1}L, and C=L intersect (u-1)^{-1}L=L intersect u^{-1}L. Applying u-1 and u to NL gives c0*n=absNorm(N^m det(u-1)) and c0*i=absNorm(N^m det u), with the same N,c0,m. The displayed bicharacter has radical exactly C; the simplification beta(wt,t)=gamma(bar(w)(ut-t),t) agrees with gauss_isometry.

HF9 supplies one actual continuous nontrivial quadratic F-idele character, principal-trivial and norm-trivial. Testing the supplied AllSome restriction against that particular character gives inert uniformizer value -1; unramifiedness removes all finite-unit factors. Infinity exponent 1/2 means phase exponent one. Principal factorization and denominator cancellation yield the exact positive product sqrt(k) times the product of absolute CM-type values, for the same half selector and the same lambda. No unspecified local sign or separate square-root choice is introduced.

The Poincare series and all real derivatives are locally uniformly and absolutely convergent: finite support is a rational-lattice coset and derivatives are polynomial times a positive Gaussian. The second phase is b(iota(a),y+x), the right magnetic translate commuting with the left Heisenberg derivatives. It therefore preserves the same Cartan vacuum. The quadratic phase identity gives corrected A-fixing and raw fixing on 2A. The family F_{-v}(iota(v)) has zero Fourier coefficient one and all nonzero rational frequencies remain nonzero, proving a nonzero vector without importing vacuum nonvanishing.

For the scalar trace identity, u-1 is a rational bijection. The finite/real character product gives exactly chi_A((u-1)y)=Q_u(y) exp(-pi*i*omega(uy,y)); the remaining phases give G_u(y+v). On the right, support of a_j(y) implies y_f+b_j is in A. Testing c in C against both A and r(p)A gives integral frequencies on C. Exactly one finite transversal representative is in A, and at that representative the two quadratic phases cancel, so sum_j a_j(0)=1. Q_u descends to B1/C, with exactly n cosets. Absolute integrability from CW20 justifies unfolding over those cosets; the sole real factor is the positive covolume of C. This is the source gauss_mul_integral normalization, not its absolute-value weakening.

The original inverse-pair action U is retained. The exponent E=1/2((U-1)^*Hs(U-1)-HU+(HU)^*) has positive Hermitian part when det(U-1) is nonzero. On the s=+1 and s=-1 blocks, direct multiplication verifies E U(P_+U^{-1}+P_-)=-H(U-1). The complex Gaussian integral is determinant(E)^{-1} times a positive coordinate Jacobian. Since det(-H)det(-s)=det(Hs)>0, this yields I*P=r2*det(-s)*Q*delta with r2 positive and the exact original real-vacuum determinant. The constant Cartan sign is not absorbed into a positive factor.

All inverse orientations were checked against scalar_const and final_algebra. The common denominator appears in both eta positivity equations. Unitarity yields Delta*bar(Delta)=1 and Delta*bar(d)=(-1)^m*d. For the one-sided cut F and two-sided cut G, G(x)F(bar(x))=F(x) and zF(Delta)=1 imply z*y2=s0*y1, with the direction written in the proof. Eliminating I,P,Q,Z,lambda(c0),lambda(i) and using lambda(n)^2=n gives c_p*epsilon0=(r1*r3/(r2*r4*n))*s0. Every cancelled factor is nonzero, and the remaining real ratio is strictly positive.

The rational norm-one scalars (a+xi)/(a-xi), a in Q, form an infinite set. Avoiding finitely many roots makes both tU-1 and tI-1 invertible. The central target pair and its product with the original pair have the same fixed Cartan sign and eta-cut sign. Multiplicativity of the scalar then makes the original scalar positive; only at this point does norm one force it to equal one. Rational quasi-reflections preserve nonisotropic lines, admit commuting Cartans, and generate the rational unitary group by WA10, yielding both factors of rational pullback and evaluation at zero. Rank-zero empty determinants and integrals are harmless.

Checked the literal eleven fields std, hecS, hecT, resS, resT, om_pres, om_heis, om_aut, om_cont, om_unit and om_split in LocalNewformFunction.lean53-75. The output extends the combined theta action once; it does not assume arbitrary independent extensions commute off the theta space. Norm equality is for each original additive Haar measure and fundamental domain. Split and nonsplit support have trivial real component, and real support has trivial finite cut; hence FixesVacAt and VacCharPlus have the exact original lattices, Cartans and determinant orientation.

The coordinate lattice is the image under the existing frame-coordinate isomorphism of the original self-dual lattice, not a replacement Gram matrix. The tensor map a tensor x -> baseAdele(a)*diag(x) is a continuous semilinear tensor map and preserves principal ideles and local support components; completion agreement follows from rational density. It transports HF11 unitary eta0 with its exact finite unramified readings, phase exponent one and explicit HF9 restriction.

The universal AllSome issue is correctly separated. The transported eta0 is not asserted to satisfy the unreconstructed uniqueness clause of IsEtaTilde. Auditing the operator argument shows that Hecke continuity/principal triviality, norm triviality, unramifiedness, explicit inert signs and the infinity phases are sufficient. The supplied ResEta(chi_S),ResEta(chi_T), tested against HF9, make chi/eta0^rank trivial on every F-idele. WA18 determinant roots then give an idele character independent of all root choices, continuous, unitary and rational-trivial, with the exact crossed split factor. The prescribed characters themselves supply the universal final restriction fields. This constructs the full datum without importing globalNormIndexTwo or the canonical existence endpoint. It does not assert the two extra canonical vacuum clauses after an arbitrary twist.

Matched bottom_chars74-95, exists_bottomTri104-134 and IsBottomTri.integrable136-147 in BottomExistsIntegrable.lean. The given level eta remains in all parity corrections; the auxiliary eta0 is only a construction tool. Negating the Hermitian form preserves the same self-dual lattice. CW24 supplies the two new full Weil families needed by WA17, on the same prescribed spaces/characters. The given grid realization is retained rather than identified with a bottom representation. WA16 supplies SumsIn for those exact triangles and original measures; finite T is explicit and follows from HidaSetting.fin in the literal NFBot context. A finite compositum over squares preserves all period and range clauses.

Dependency review found no new circle. CW20 uses the earlier matrix/Gaussian identities and CW17, not CW19; CW19 may therefore use its integrability. The scalar argument treats a zero theta space harmlessly until the independently constructed nonzero family gives uniqueness. CW24 reuses the inspected operator formulas under weaker explicit eta properties rather than invoking the stronger IsEtaTilde endpoint. WA17 and WA18 remain inherited conditional statements; CW24/CW25 discharge their representation input without modifying inherited claims.
